rounds.text: Borana Weaves trades at a modest P/E of 13.6x [E1], which is dramatically discounted compared to the broader sector benchmark P/E of 31.12x [E6], while delivering exceptional profitability highlighted by a 35.0% ROE and a 32.7% ROCE [E13, E12] that dwarf the sector medians of 10.03% and 7.6% respectively [E9, E67]. This fundamental outperformance is backed by phenomenal recent growth, including 34% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E15], a 58% surge in trailing profits [E17], and expanding operating margins that reached 25% in the March 2026 quarter [E23]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 990 per share, offering a striking 66.9% margin of safety against the market price of Rs 328 [E37, E38], with a reverse DCF implying that the current price merely prices in a modest 2.8% earnings growth rate [E39]. Management is proactively cementing this competitive advantage by commissioning a 19.79 MW Solar-Wind Hybrid Power Project to supply 70 to 80 percent of power needs [E74, E70], alongside an aggressive expansion roadmap targeting 2,000 looms by March 2028 [E89]. Conceded: free cash flow stands at a negative Rs 142 Cr for March 2026 [E28] and institutional money flow registers as negative [E36].

Despite reported profit growth, Borana Weaves Ltd suffers from severe cash flow disconnects, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.57x and operating cash flow representing only 41% of operating profit as of March 2026 [E26, E29]. This shortfall translates into a staggering negative free cash flow of minus 142 crore rupees for March 2026 [E28], driven by a sharp deterioration in working capital days from 57.0 days to 86.5 days [E55] and potential capitalization of interest costs [E54]. Compounding these fundamental financial strains, institutional confidence is evaporating, marked by a negative money flow signal [E36], foreign institutional holdings dropping from 3.55% to 1.66% [E34], and domestic institutional holdings falling from 6.98% to 2.78% [E35]. Furthermore, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% despite its repeated profits [E4, E53], and faces clear warnings of decelerating earnings growth [E61]. Conceded: the company demonstrates high reported return on equity figures and sales growth alongside a low price-to-earnings ratio compared to the sector benchmark [E1, E9, E13, E14, E57].

Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.57x and operating cash flow is 41% of operating profit as of March 2026 [E26, E29], alongside a negative free cash flow of minus 142 crore rupees [E28] and an increase in working capital days to 86.5 days [E55]. However, the negative free cash flow and cash flow disconnect directly stem from heavy, deliberate capital allocation toward future growth, specifically strategic capacity expansion plans designed to double loom capacity from 1,000 to 2,000 looms by March 2028 [E76, E89]. Conceded: institutional holdings have declined and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E34, E35, E53], but this zero payout reflects a deliberate retention of capital to fund this high-return expansion rather than underlying business distress. This reinvestment strategy is entirely justified by elite return metrics, including an ROE of 35.0% and ROCE of 32.7% [E12, E13], outperforming sector medians significantly [E9, E10]. Furthermore, operating margins are expanding rather than deteriorating, increasing to 24% in March 2026 with an increasing multi-year trend [E22, E24], supported by newly commissioned renewable energy projects expected to further boost efficiency [E69, E74].
